import java.util.Scanner;

public class I {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        Scanner s = new Scanner(System.in);
        long n = s.nextLong();
        double p = s.nextDouble();
        solve(n, p);
    }

    public static void solve(long n, double p) {
        long studied = 0;
        long notStudied = n;

        while (true) {
            long totalWays = nCr(n, 3);
            
            // Calculate favorable cases
            long favorable = 0;
            
            // Case 1: 0 studied maps in the 3 selected
            if (notStudied >= 3) {
                long zeroStudied = nCr(notStudied, 3);
                // In this case, Johnny can't pick a studied map, so probability = 0
                favorable += 0;
            }
            
            // Case 2: 1 studied map in the 3 selected
            if (studied >= 1 && notStudied >= 2) {
                long oneStudied = nCr(studied, 1) * nCr(notStudied, 2);
                // Johnny picks the studied map (1 choice), opponent picks randomly among 3
                // System picks from remaining 2 maps that weren't picked by either player
                // If Johnny picks studied, opponent can pick any of the 3
                // Maps not picked by either: if Johnny picks studied, opponent picks one of 2 not studied
                // Then system picks from the remaining 1 not studied map
                // So probability = 1/3 (Johnny picks studied) * 1 (opponent picks one of others) * 1/2 (system picks from remaining 1)
                // Actually: Johnny picks studied (1/3), opponent picks one of the 2 not studied (2/3 chance), 
                // then system picks from the remaining 1 not studied map (1 map left unpicked)
                // But if opponent also picks studied (1/3), system picks from 2 not studied
                // Let's recalculate: 
                // Johnny picks studied (prob 1/3), opponent picks randomly among 3
                //   - opponent picks studied (1/3): system picks from 2 not studied -> 0 chance for studied
                //   - opponent picks not studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 not studied -> 0 chance for studied
                // Johnny picks not studied (2/3), opponent picks randomly among 3
                //   - opponent picks studied (1/3): system picks from remaining 1 not studied -> 0 chance
                //   - opponent picks not studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 map (could be studied or not studied)
                //     If Johnny picked not studied, opponent picked not studied, then remaining is studied -> 1/1 chance
                // So probability = (2/3) * (2/3) * 1 = 4/9
                // Actually simpler: system picks randomly from maps not picked by either player
                // With 1 studied and 2 not studied: 
                // Johnny's strategy: pick studied if available
                // Opponent picks randomly
                // Cases:
                // - Johnny picks studied (1/3), opponent picks studied (1/3): system picks from 2 not studied -> 0
                // - Johnny picks studied (1/3), opponent picks not studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 not studied -> 0
                // - Johnny picks not studied (2/3), opponent picks studied (1/3): system picks from remaining 1 not studied -> 0
                // - Johnny picks not studied (2/3), opponent picks not studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 map (studied) -> 1
                // So probability = (2/3)*(2/3)*1 = 4/9
                favorable += oneStudied * 4; // 4/9 * 9 = 4 (we'll multiply by 9 later to avoid fractions)
            }
            
            // Case 3: 2 studied maps in the 3 selected
            if (studied >= 2 && notStudied >= 1) {
                long twoStudied = nCr(studied, 2) * nCr(notStudied, 1);
                // Johnny picks one of the 2 studied (2/3), opponent picks randomly
                // - opponent picks studied (1/3): system picks from 1 not studied -> 0
                // - opponent picks not studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 studied -> 1
                // Johnny picks not studied (1/3), opponent picks randomly
                // - opponent picks studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 studied -> 1
                // - opponent picks not studied (1/3): system picks from remaining 2 studied -> 1
                // Probability = (2/3)*(2/3)*1 + (1/3)*(2/3)*1 + (1/3)*(1/3)*1 = 4/9 + 2/9 + 1/9 = 7/9
                favorable += twoStudied * 7;
            }
            
            // Case 4: 3 studied maps in the 3 selected
            if (studied >= 3) {
                long threeStudied = nCr(studied, 3);
                // Johnny picks studied (1/3), opponent picks randomly
                // - opponent picks studied (2/3): system picks from remaining 1 studied -> 1
                // - opponent picks studied (1/3, same as Johnny): system picks from remaining 2 studied -> 1
                // Actually: all maps are studied, so whatever system picks is studied
                // Probability = 1
                favorable += threeStudied * 9; // 1 = 9/9
            }
            
            // Check if favorable/total >= p
            // favorable is calculated with denominator 9, so favorable/9/total >= p
            // => favorable >= 9 * p * total
            if (favorable >= 9 * p * totalWays) {
                System.out.println(studied);
                return;
            }
            
            studied++;
            notStudied--;
        }
    }

    private static long nCr(long n, long r) {
        if (r > n || r < 0) return 0;
        if (r == 0 || r == n) return 1;
        if (r == 1) return n;
        if (r == 2) return n * (n - 1) / 2;
        if (r == 3) return n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) / 6;
        return 0;
    }
}
